messages:
priya: heads-up: scheduling rollout for runtime v3.0-quantC tonight. change: new fused-matmul kernel + reordered launches. staging smoke passed but a few long-tail p99 spikes showed up on large-batch tests.

misha: saw the p99 spikes too. repro with `--batch-size=128 --seq=256` locally, looks like kernel launch serialization under older drivers.

lee: clarifying note: kernel relies on CUDA stream semantics available in driver 510+. older drivers 470/495 can still run but need the compatibility shim. shim is safe but slower.

sam: request: please do NOT flip the fleet-wide rollout. plan: canary 1% in eu-west-1b, limit to instance-family g5/g6 with driver>=510. if green 20m, step +3% every 15m. fallback: full rollback to v2.9.8 if error-rate > 0.7% OR p95 latency > baseline*1.25 for 10m.

priya: agreed. added note to release notes draft: https://wiki.redwood/release/RT-3.0.0-quantC (section: driver/shim guidance).

deploybot: preflight: image runtime:v3.0-quantC uploaded, checksums OK. suggested command: `/deploy runtime --image runtime:v3.0-quantC --canary 1 --step 3 --step-interval 900 --selector instance_family=g5,driver>=510 --monitor p95,errors`

opsbot: quick smoke tail: `kubectl exec -it pod/runtime-abc -- tail -n 200 /var/log/runtime.log | grep -i "kernel launch"` returned intermittent "kernel timeout" traces on one eu-west-1a dev node. not in canary pool (eu-west-1b).

misha: hold canary until we verify driver/firmware on canary nodes. I can push a small probe job: `kubectl run driver-check --image=redwood/tools:latest --restart=OnFailure -- sh -c "nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version --format=csv"`

lee: do the probe and also tag nodes with label `driver_ok=true` if >=510. deploybot can accept `--node-selector driver_ok=true` for the canary.

priya: doing probe now. will tag nodes and then start canary. ETA 8m.

(deploybot): probe job created at 1746500240. results pending.

opsbot: probe results: 6/6 candidate nodes in eu-west-1b report driver 510.47 and above. tagging `driver_ok=true` on them.

priya: tagging complete. will kick off canary in 2m.

jess: add a note in release notes about performance delta with shim: "Nodes on older drivers will use the compatibility shim and may see +10-20% latency on large batches." Also call out rollback criteria and who to page.

priya: added. also included recommended mitigation steps: (1) pin older fleets with `deploybot pin --selector driver<510 --version v2.9.8 --ttl 6h`, (2) ops contact to schedule driver upgrade waves, (3) doc link to hotpatch path.

deploybot: canary started at 1746500380 -> slice: eu-west-1b, selector: driver_ok=true, traffic=1%. monitoring endpoints: /metrics/runtime and /healthz. roll plan: 1% -> 4% -> 7% -> 10% (15m between steps).

sam: monitoring hooks set: p50/p95/p99, errors, gpu-util, kernel-timeout-count. alerts: p95 > baseline*1.25 for 5m; errors +0.5% absolute for 5m; kernel-timeout-count > 5 per minute.

(priya): initial 10m: p95 +2%, errors flat, gpu-util normal, kernel-timeout-count = 0. rolling to 4%.

misha: during 2nd step saw a single pod restart with `SIGABRT` and log excerpt: ```
E runtime: matmul-fused: launch failed: out_of_memory at /src/kernel/launch.c:212
stack: ...
```

opsbot: pod restart trace on canary: `oom_kill` but memory pressure not high cluster-wide. investigating cgroup settings on that host.

lee: remote host had custom cgroup tunables (reserve=0). Ops, can we set reserve to 200MB on canary hosts?

opsbot: applied cgroup reserve tweak to canary nodes at 1746500600.

sam: re-eval after tweak: p95 back to +1%, errors 0.15% (within threshold). kernel-timeout-count 0.

priya: green for 20m now. continue to 7% and observe another 20m. jess, can you review the release note driver section for wording?

jess: wording looks good. call-out: "If you see repeated SIGABRTs referencing matmul-fused, immediately pause rollout and tag @eng-runtime on-call."

priya: continuing. final check: if any node in rollout reports driver<510 unexpectedly, auto-pause. deploybot will enforce.

deploybot: auto-pause rule applied: pause if node label driver_ok!=true detected in rollout slice.

misha: two follow-ups: (1) record a short postdeploy checklist for ops to verify cgroup knobs after driver upgrades, (2) plan a small canary in us-east later once driver waves complete.

priya: noted. wrapping up thread 1: will unpin older drivers after ops confirms upgrade schedule. thanks team :rocket:
